correctness.rationale: For kappa(n)=1+sum_{d|n,d<n} kappa(d), kappa depends only on prime exponent tuple. Replacing distinct odd primes with (3,5,7) weakly lowers n while preserving kappa, so any smaller odd three-support ample n yields a smaller canonical ample triple. The rational exponent generating function 1/[2(1-x)(1-y)(1-z)-1] gives an exact seven-neighbor recurrence. A separately implemented multidimensional prefix recurrence independently exhausts ALL 4650 positive canonical triples with 3^a5^b7^c<=801204488268064453125: all 4649 strictly smaller have kappa<=n and the sole boundary triple (20,9,6) yields kappa=841632661765951062016>n. Odd numbers with <=2 prime supports have sigma(n)/n<=15/8<2, are deficient, and by proper-divisor induction cannot be ample. Uniqueness at minimum follows strict increase of the product under larger primes.
residual_risks: An unindexed tabulation or unpublished exact minimum with three prime supports could predate this finite census.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Fink introduced recursive-divisor ample numbers and recorded the least odd ample integer without support constraint, on five prime supports; that does not determine the minimum at exactly three supports. The published finite-prime-support theorem proves existential infinitely many ample numbers if Euler product>2 but expressly has no effective least-witness bound. The explicit threshold and uniqueness are strictly finer than existence. Stronger generic/family theorems were compared by their actual implications rather than title alone; these listed results do not give the particular new invariant.
